text:
alex: heads up, hit a correctness blip in prod during rolling maintenance. two nodes briefly believed they owned the same prefix and we saw duplicate read paths.

maria: yikes. can you paste the short timeline?

alex: sure: node A heartbeat jitter -> controller moves claim -> node B requests snapshot -> node A still returned reads for ~150ms while B applied snapshot -> some routers sent reads to both.

sam: this is the classic race between claim+apply and inflight-serving. we need a lightweight mechanism so routers don't flip ownership mid-flight.

jen: any chance this was caused by slow demote on node A? we saw GC pauses yesterday on that instance.

alex: yes GC spikes made demote acknowledgements slow. Node A replied to snapshot request with "ok apply" but didn't stop serving immediately. B applied then both served stale+new.

ralph: option 1: require a fence token during snapshot apply (CAS). node with older token must stop serving before a new apply succeeds. avoids double-serve but adds an RTT to claim.

sam: option 2: lightweight redirect header. when a node intends to hand off, it responds with x-prefix-redirect: node-A for a short TTL and routers cache mapping. New owner waits for redirect TTL to expire before becoming authoritative.

jen: redirect avoids extra round trips on claim path. downside: routers need to check cached redirects on every read -> must be fast and bounded.

alex: what about a hybrid: claim publishes "pending" ownership in control-plane (cheap) -> routers treat pending as hint and consult primary shard map; if they see pending they add one conditional check to call target node which can reply with either serve/redirect/readonly status. replies include an expiry ms.

maria: that makes ownership transitions explicit and observable. we should also add standard error code for transient ownership: 503 PREFIX_OWNERSHIP_TRANSITION + metadata {owner,node_ts,expiry_ms}. apps can surface a retry.

sam: implementation notes: make snapshot apply idempotent. include last_applied_seq and incoming_snapshot_seq in apply request. if apply_seq <= last_applied_seq, ignore. that prevents double-apply during races.

jen: config knobs prototype: 
```
prefetch.claim_delay_ms = 100   # wait after claim before active if redirect present
prefetch.redirect_ttl_ms = 75   # routers cache redirect entries
prefetch.max_pending_ms = 2000  # how long a claim can stay pending before forcing read-only
```

ralph: telemetry: add prefix_ownership_state transitions, redirect_cache_hit, demote_ack_time_ms, owner_last_heartbeat_ms. we'll need these to tune claim_delay per region.

alex: ops-bot: schedule canary rollout?

ops-bot: canary planned: shardpool-canary-7 on 2026-03-23T04:00Z. config will include redirect_ttl_ms=75 and claim_delay_ms=100. alert: demote_ack_time_ms > 150ms.

maria: test plan: inject hotkey traffic while simulating GC pause on old owner. verify redirect hit ratio and no duplicate-serving. also test split-brain: old owner unreachable but still marked as serving -> new owner should enter read-only and return the new 503 code.

sam: we should also update router impl to avoid expensive global locks on redirects. use a small LRU with 128 entries and atomic swap for updates.

jen: I'll write a short RFC addendum with state diagram: UNCLAIMED -> PENDING -> PASSIVE_SYNC -> ACTIVE. document behavior of routers and error code semantics.

ralph: ops: add dashboard with prefix_ownership_state and demote_ack_time_ms. correlate with p99 latency.

alex: actionable list: 1) jen drafts RFC addendum (with sequence diagram) 2) sam implements idempotent apply + LRU redirect cache 3) ralph + maria add metrics and dashboards 4) alex define 503 payload shape + library helpers for SDKs

jen: note: keep redirects short. too long and we hurt new owner activation for hotkeys. too short and we may not prevent duplicate-serving. defaults above are a starting point.

alex: thanks team. will follow-up with RFC link when ready. end.
